newsitem.title: UK: Options-Coffee rally sparks big trades, cocoa idles.
newsitem.headline: Options-Coffee rally sparks big trades, cocoa idles.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures' surge this week to about a one-year high has fired up options speculators looking for a way to ride the next wave up, analysts said.

"There's been big interest in out-of-the-money calls in July, September and even, November," said an analyst. "There's been activity across the board, the whole range. The market's setting up for further gains."

Some put buying to hedge long positions has emerged as some investors become nervous that the recent, quick climb to dizzying heights could correct just as fast. But analysts said most of the activity has remained on the call side.

Speculators have been snatching up calls, most notably at the $1,950, $2,000 and $2,300 strikes in September and November. Trade houses, particularly one large one, has been offering those out-of-the-money calls relatively cheaply near 45 percent, a trader said.
Implied July coffee volatility closed near 44 percent and September near 45 percent on Wednesday. Both were up sharply from last week's levels near 38 and 39 percent, respectively.

If coffee futures extend gains toward those strikes and tread into even higher, unfamiliar ground, traders said options-related activity in the futures could heat up, especially if the large trade house that heavily sold calls at the $2,000 and $2,300 strikes was not fully hedged.

If the out-of-the-money call sales are not fully hedged and underlying futures rise to put those calls in the money, the trade house might be forced to buy massive amounts of futures to stay even, which would further feed a buying frenzy.

More action is also expected to come with every volatility spike higher as futures break new ground, traders said. They said volatility traders have also entered the fray, hoping for even greater volatililty.
If frost in Brazil surfaces, traders said that, coupled with the tight supplies, would likely be enough to send prices and volatilities soaring.

While coffee has enjoyed the burst of activity, cocoa has had to sit on the sidelines and watch. Traders saw very little interest in cocoa options as the underlying futures continue to trade in a tight range amid lacklustre volume.

Implied cocoa volatility has eased with the lack of activity in the underlying futures, traders said. They pegged July near 28 percent and September just slightly higher at 29 percent. They expected volatillity to continue slipping as long as cocoa paces up and down its trading range.
